pr_title: Add NC, SCTP support and stages to Jig verifier
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Fixes #94598

- Test jig method vs functions arent really needed as they're al internal to the Jig stuff
- The addition of test methods to to Jig mean that they can reuse the client and other fixtures we might eventually add
- We need SCTP verification as well

This might allow us to also use the JIG as the driver in the netpol test that is going on, and is part of an overall effort to make the E2Es more fixture driven for better reasoning over time.

/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adding SCTP support to Test-jig and having it pre-verify execution target

Might be adopted in #91592

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```
pr_comments:
> 
> Test jig method vs functions arent really needed as they're al internal to the Jig stuff
> The addition of test methods to to Jig mean that they can reuse the client and other fixtures we might eventually add

I defer to framework maintainers the decision, but shouldn't be better to move functions to methods when we have a reason to do that?  
I mean, it may happen that we want to export the functions in the future :shrug:

> > Test jig method vs functions arent really needed as they're al internal to the Jig stuff
> > The addition of test methods to to Jig mean that they can reuse the client and other fixtures we might eventually add
> 
> I mean, it may happen that we want to export the functions in the future shrug

The reason it *seems to me* like these should all be TestJig methods, rather then standalone, is so that they can reuse the TestJig functionality (including client, so that preverification of pod states can happen before running `exec` statements and so on).

There is a workaround - we can plumb the client manually into testServiceReachability... and then have a wrapper func in TestJig? But that seems silly since the *only* reference to these functions is *from* the TestJig, and likely we'll be moving *more* towards a higher level fixture type tests over time as opposed to 'roll your own' style tests, hence the idea that you need to depend on TestJig for this functionality seems idiomatic to me... and also because, after all, the entire file is named *jig.go* :)

issue_context.title: Update agnhost nc version, add support for SCTP to TestJig
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:

- functionality for TestJig fixture might be able to be reused in var (example #91592)  (example #91592) ious emerging fixture based tests and the jig.go file should unify the functions under the Jig struct (so as to be able to add defensive checks in tests and so on that use the client of the jig).
- functionality to the agnhost to support sctp via newer nc versions since its a commonly used polling tool in k8s e2e.

**Why is this needed**:


- SCTP support to the TestJig as well  (example #91592 which creates pod fixtures and then polls them needs to fully support SCTP).
- as @aojea  points out, some containers (Such as current `agnhost`) dont have an `nc` version which supports `--sctp`.  This can i think easily be fixed by replacing the `apk` install from `netcat-openbsd` (which is old, 2017) to `nmap-netcat` (2019).  Since these all alias to the same `nc` command, its not going to change the way other tests need to run.

review_comments:
you can use `isInvalidOrLocalhostAddress()` or 	
```
parsedIP := net.ParseIP(ip)
	if parsedIP == nil 
```
(move of the earlier code) but valid point i think

what netcat version is this? the one provided in the agnhost  image used by most of the test does not have this option
```
 nc -h
OpenBSD netcat (Debian patchlevel 1.130)
```

To answer your specific question - `nc`as `ncat > 7.8` will work... but as you said, all pods wont have this.  

Luckily,  This function takes the pod as *input* so wether or not an `nc` tool is present isn't actually a constraint on this functions implementation .  That said you are right, many pods might not support the `--sctp` option.  However *some pods* will (specifically, we need to support this for sure in #91592, so we'll make sure of that)

Either way since the pod is an input to the system, i think its valid if sctp fails.

Looking more

- it looks like `netcat-openbsd` doesnt support sctp
- `netcat` the regular package *does* support sctp

But again, this function's ability to use sctp is going to be container dependent, regardless, and so it seems like its reasonable to say ' if the pod has an the current version of  nc, this will work, if it has an older version, it might not work'.
Trying this out in a related issue #96482 . Once you install the nmap-netcat, does it symlink `nc` to `ncat` ?
Yup it does (correct me if I'm wrong here been a few months since I put this patch up)

I don't think that it did, at least when I tried the test with your change to the Docker image, it just seemed to pickup the nc that is installed in BusyBox. 

I added the changes and tried to use the new ncat explicitly in the following branch that you can try out https://github.com/cmluciano/kubernetes/tree/cml/testnchelp

`export KUBE_TEST_REPO_LIS=$GOPATH/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/repo_list.yaml`
```bazel build //test/e2e:e2e.test && \
 cd src/k8s.io/kubernetes/bazel-out/k8-fastbuild-ST-77d62fd15d15fc7ab69058da1afba983b16c05cd7d7cd724cce6b37445e7a9d1/bin/test/e2e/e2e.test_ \
&& ./e2e.test -context kind-kind -ginkgo.focus="RunUdpTest" -ginkgo.trace```

When I try that out, my output shows nc pointing to the busybox version and it is symlinked to the normal `/usr/bin/nc`.

Why are we using the -z option here? Is there a noted reason to not send data? Also I'm wondering if we want to move away from netcat in general in favor of agnhost. Agnhost seems to better align with the way many connections in NetPol are tested [test/e2e/network/network_policy.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1c403c311e80dcdb075219d117ac803f8891de39/test/e2e/network/network_policy.go#L2049-L2051)
In favor of agn host but I thought we still used nc in various places.  As long as we do use it.  The ability to use NCat (as opposed to the old netcat) gives us parity between sctp udp tcp ....
A quck scan for `nc -` matches in the codebase point toward main uses for udp port checking. This likely is due to agnhost connect cannot be used for UDP.
